dedupe_keys.name: tracking the sun project level data on installed prices and characteristics of us distributed solar pv systems lbnl

description: Tracking the Sun is the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report series and dataset on installed prices and other characteristics of grid-connected distributed solar PV systems in the United States. The data come mainly from project-level records held by state agencies and utilities that run PV incentive programmes, renewable energy credit registries or interconnection processes. According to the federal catalogue entry, the latest report is based on 3.2 million systems installed through 2022, over 80 percent of systems installed to date, while the OEDI submission describes the 2018 edition with more than 1.3 million systems. Records cover system size and design, ownership, customer segment, installer, module efficiency, inverter technology, mounting, new construction or retrofit and installed price; distributed PV means roof-mounted systems of any size and ground-mounted systems up to 5 MWAC. Data are available as a free download from the Open Energy Data Initiative data lake on AWS without sign-in, with a GitHub documentation page, an interactive tool and report PDFs; the licence is CC BY 4.0 and the entry was modified on 18 June 2024. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: coverage depends on state programmes, and the LBNL pages refused automated reading on the day. Simulation uses are distributed PV locations, sizes and inverter types for feeder hosting capacity and adoption models.
